An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf retr 19
div.ab: De uxoribus malefactorum et filiis eorum. Si quidem tales habuerint uxores suas in patria subsistentes, et dixerit aliquis parentum murdriti, eas nequitie fuisse participes, expurgent se iudicio Dei.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 644 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

div.ab: Of the wives of evildoers and their sons. If indeed such men have their wives remaining in the country, and any of the kinsmen of the murdered man says that they were sharers in the wickedness, let them clear themselves by the judgment of God.
